question.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1),\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1)=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1} & \frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\operatorname{ln}⁡6,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\operatorname{ln}⁡6=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡6+(-\frac{1}{3})+\frac{2}{3}=\operatorname{ln}⁡6+\frac{1}{3}.
$$
